Dear Colleague,

I am writing to provide a comprehensive summary of my consultation with Ms. Victoria Banks, which took place on January 6, 2026, at our clinic. Ms. Banks was referred to me due to her BRCA/Lynch positive status with no evidence of cancer at this time.

Upon reviewing Ms. Banks' history, it is clear that her BRCA/Lynch positive condition has been managed effectively, and she currently exhibits no of malignancy. During the consultation, I confirmed that she is not on any medications specifically for this condition. 

During the physical examination, Ms. Banks' vital signs were within normal limits with a blood pressure of 136/76 mmHg and a weight of 138 pounds. Other findings from her examination were unremarkable, and she reported no new symptoms related to her BRCA/Lynch status. She did mention a mild headache but attributed it to recent stress.

Socially, Ms. Banks disclosed that she was a former cigarette smoker, having smoked half a pack per day starting from April Z8, 1991, and quitting on March 23, 1995. She has been honest about her smoking history and does not currently use any tobacco products.

Given her controlled BRCA/Lynch status and otherwise normal physical examination, my impression is that Ms. Banks is managing her condition well with no current need for additional interventions. I recommend continuing regular follow-up to monitor her status and ensure that any potential symptoms are promptly addressed.

Thank you for referring Ms. Banks to our clinic. I appreciate your collaboration in her ongoing care.

Sincerely,

Dr. Madison Jenkins
